candidates.changed_node: TS_MIN($low, 21) -> TS_MIN($low, 63) (the range floor, both occurrences)
candidates.rationale: Weakness is the monotone IC decay (+0.0250 in 2000 to +0.0010 in 2013) against a 19.3-day IC half-life: the 21-day floor is rebuilt well inside the signal's own horizon, and once ranges compressed after 2003 the box collapsed and the score saturated at 0/1. Holding the floor at 63 days gives a drawdown reference that outlives the half-life while the 21-day ceiling keeps the reading current; changing the node that appears in both numerator and denominator also breaks the shared subtree that left this 0.608-correlated with the archive.

The price leg is normalized by a price level, so it is just percent-above-the-21-day-low, which ranks high-volatility names highest and imports a raw vol tilt. That leg, not the fundamental one, drags 2012 negative (RANK($roa) alone is +0.0061 that year while the composite is -0.0012) and deepens 2003. Measuring the same distance in 21-day sigma removes the vol tilt and drops the factor from 4 fields to 3, which also removes the 0.100 complexity charge.

Coverage 0.904 sits only 0.004 above the hard gate and is set by the longest window, the 189-day high; that is the binding risk on this factor. The same 9-month reference is also stale right after a regime turn, which is what makes 2003 and 2013 the two negative years. Cutting it to 63 days restores coverage headroom (the 126-day vol leg becomes binding) and turns the leg into a live drawdown measure at a horizon consistent with the 19.7-day half-life.

Raw $volume is a share-count level, i.e. a size/liquidity characteristic: that is why its IC never halves inside 63 days and why it sits at rho 0.717 against the archived TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21). The level is what makes it redundant, not what makes it predictive, while the daily spikes on top of it pay 0.153 turnover. Ranking volume against its own 126-day history strips the level, keeps the slow horizon the half-life implies, and separates it from the archived dollar-volume level and 21-day z-score factors.

The $roa level is a static characteristic (turnover 0.007, 43.2-day half-life) already spanned by the archive at rho 0.737, and re-dressing it has failed before, so the level itself is the weak node. It is negative in exactly the two re-rating years, 2003 and 2006, when the market paid for improving rather than high profitability. A 126-day change in ROA is one long fundamental window (the size that cleared coverage previously) and is close to orthogonal to the archived level rank.

IC half-life 4.9 days against 0.177 daily turnover: the numerator is a single bar's range, so the factor re-ranks every day on noise that cannot predict a week ahead, while the accrual leg it is multiplying is quarterly. A 5-day mean range keeps the accrual-times-normalized-range vein and the 21-day denominator intact, gives the untried 5/21 window mix, and uses TS_MEAN rather than the archived sibling's TS_SUM($high - $low, 5) form so no 4-node subtree is reproduced.

Stability 0.71 is the worst in the population and the failure is a clean regime block, not scattered noise: 2007, 2009, 2010 and 2011 all negative after six straight positive years. That is book-to-price's lost decade, driven by book value that was not marked in financials, so the value leg is the weak node. Swapping the numerator to earnings per share keeps the price-scaled-fundamental plus quality-rank structure that scored here and replaces book yield with an earnings yield that stayed informative through the credit period.

Turnover 0.291 against a 40.3-day IC half-life is the clearest mismatch here: the second leg re-ranks daily off one bar while the information it carries lasts a month, so it pays costs for churn it does not earn back. The one-bar form is also what leaves it at rho 0.765 against the archived accrual sibling, uncomfortably close to the 0.80 gate. Averaging the range-to-open ratio over 21 days matches the leg to the half-life and moves it away from the sibling's 2- and 5-day windows.

candidates.changed_node: the 2-day window on the efficiency ratio -> 10 days (TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_SUM)
candidates.rationale: The 2-day window is the weak component: turnover 0.656 costs 0.022 of a 2.661 fitness, the IC half-life is 3.4 days, and stability is 0.71, all symptoms of a microstructure reading being scored against a longer horizon. Widening the same efficiency ratio to 10 days preserves the construction and its 0.212 archive distance, cuts the turnover charge by roughly an order of magnitude, and avoids the archived TS_SUM($high - $low, 5) subtree that a 5-day version would reproduce.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Budget one long time-series term per candidate. A single 126d fundamental delta was accepted (1.589), but two 126d fundamental deltas combined, or any 252d window on $roa/$roe/$return, landed at 0.869-0.882 coverage.
  2. Stop submitting CS_ZSCORE times CS_ZSCORE products. Both died on the cheap screen (leverage x TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) at 0.57, 5d return reversal x $roe at 0.59). The accepted mixed factors use a cross-sectional fundamental rank as the base and a raw price ratio as the multiplier.
  3. Pure price-geometry expressions with no fundamental field were the worst cheap-screen scores of the round (0.36 and 0.41). Do not send TS_MAX/TS_MIN/high-low range constructions unless a fundamental score leads the expression.
  4. $accrual_gap times a normalized intraday range is this island's best vein (3.570 and 2.250 accepted). Extend it by varying the window structure of the range and its normalizer (2/5/21 day mixes), not by swapping the denominator's scale, which returned rho 0.839 against an archived sibling.
  5. Re-dressing an archived factor never clears correlation: raw $roa against RANK($roa) is 1.000, and attaching a strictly positive bounded range multiplier to RANK($roa) still leaves rho 0.860. To decorrelate from a single-field archived rank, subtract a second cross-sectional rank or change sign structure instead of multiplying.
  6. Price-scaling a fundamental and adding a plain quality rank works ($book_per_share/$open with $roe scored 3.155), but pairing a price-scaled fundamental with a 252d volatility term failed coverage at 0.869. Keep the second leg a contemporaneous cross-sectional rank.
  7. Crossover needs a real subtree splice. Two proposals scored only 2 shared nodes because they wrapped a whole parent in a fresh multiplier; each parent should contribute a named field plus its own transform.
  8. Keep a within-round proposal ledger for the $roa and $accrual_gap templates. A roa-delta minus return-mean pair was proposed twice and burned a slot as a duplicate.

Return exactly one mutation per parent, 10 in total.
